messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Ozempic Dosing Information:
Ozempic Injection Recommended Dosage:
Start Ozempic with a 0.25 mg subcutaneous injection (injection under the skin) once weekly for 4 weeks.
The 0.25 mg dosage is intended for treatment initiation.
It is not effective for glycemic control.
After 4 weeks on the 0.25 mg dosage, increase the dosage to 0.5 mg once weekly.
If additional glycemic control is needed after at least 4 weeks on the 0.5 mg dosage.
The dosage may be increased to 1 mg once weekly.
If additional glycemic control is needed after at least 4 weeks on the 1 mg dosage.
The dosage may be increased to 2 mg once weekly.
The maximum recommended dosage is 2 mg once weekly.
Administer Ozempic once weekly, on the same day each week, at any time of the day, with or without meals.
The day of weekly administration can be changed if necessary.
The time between two doses must be at least 2 days (>48 hours).
If a dose is missed, administer Ozempic as soon as possible within 5 days after the missed dose.
If more than 5 days have passed, skip the missed dose.
Triplet: ["Ozempic", "has limitation", "not effective for glycemic control"]

The relation 'has limitation' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug is not suitable or effective for the specific use or condition described by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'not chemically related to': The subject drug is not chemically similar to or related to the substance specified by the object entity.
B. 'will not relieve': The subject drug is ineffective in alleviating or treating the condition or symptom specified by the object entity.
C. 'not used for': The subject drug is not indicated or used for the condition, situation, or purpose specified by the object entity.
D. 'not interchangeable with': The subject drug cannot be substituted directly for the drug specified by the object entity.
E. 'not approved for': The subject drug is not approved or not recommended for use in the patient population specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
